title: Sobolev boundedness of bundle symbol operators
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and positive volume form. Let $B,C$ be smooth finite-rank real vector bundles with smooth positive definite fibre metrics; their ranks need not agree. For $j\geq0$, let $H^j(B)$ be the subspace of measurable square-integrable sections modulo almost-everywhere equality whose local frame coefficients have distributional derivatives of order at most $j$ locally in $L^2$, and similarly for $C$. Use norms obtained from fixed finite smooth coordinate trivializations and subordinate smooth partitions with compact support in the charts: sum the squared Euclidean $L^2$ norms of all localized derivatives through order $j$ and take the square root. For $j=0$ use the usual integrated $L^2$ norm. Regard these sections as distributions by integration against tests. Let $r\in\mathbf Z$ and $A\in\Psi^r(B,C)$ in the sense of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. For every integer $t\geq0$ with $t-r\geq0$, the distributional restriction of $A$ is a bounded real-linear map $$A:H^t(B)\longrightarrow H^{t-r}(C).$$ In particular, there is $M_{A,t}>0$, depending only on the operator, the geometry, the chosen norms and $t$, such that $$Au\in H^{t-r}(C),\qquad\|Au\|_{H^{t-r}(C)}\leq M_{A,t}\|u\|_{H^t(B)}\quad(u\in H^t(B)).$$ The output in this assertion is the distributional action of the original $A$ on $u$, rather than an unrelated extension from smooth sections.

proof.text: Put $s=t-r\geq0$ and $\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. For a smooth compactly supported complex vector function $f$, apply the two Schwartz Fourier identities repeatedly in the coordinate directions. They give $\|f\|_{W^{j,2}}^2=\int p_j(\xi)|\widehat f(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$, where $p_j(\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq j}(2\pi)^{2|\alpha|}\xi^{2\alpha}$. Expanding $(1+\sum\xi_k^2)^j$ shows that $p_j$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $\langle\xi\rangle^{2j}$. Thus $\|f\|_{W^{j,2}}$ and $\|\langle\xi\rangle^j\widehat f\|_2$ are equivalent, also for $j=0$. Smooth compactly supported functions are Schwartz because each derivative is bounded on its compact support and vanishes off that support.

In one localized term $L_i=\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i$ of the current defining representation, keep both spatial cutoffs. Absorb the output cutoff into the symbol and extend by zero to get $b(x,\zeta)=\chi_i(x)a_i(x,\zeta)$. Its support in $x$ lies in one compact set; Leibniz and the defining local symbol bounds give all global symbol bounds required by the compact-symbol frequency-kernel lemma. For smooth compactly supported $f=\psi_i u$ that lemma identifies the actual localized quantization with $T_bf$ and its Fourier transform. Set $h(\xi)=\langle\xi\rangle^t\widehat f(\xi)$. The weighted output transform is the integral operator with matrix kernel $G(\eta,\xi)=\langle\eta\rangle^s\widehat b_x(\eta-\xi,2\pi\xi)\langle\xi\rangle^{-t}$. Its norm is at most $C_L(1+|\eta-\xi|)^{-L+s}$, since $r-t=-s$ and $\langle\eta\rangle/\langle\xi\rangle\leq2(1+|\eta-\xi|)$. Choose an integer $L>m+s$. The majorant has finite integral $I$: on $2^k\leq|z|<2^{k+1}$ its integral is at most a fixed multiple of $2^{k(m-L+s)}$, a convergent geometric series, and on the unit ball it is bounded. Translation invariance gives both Schur marginal bounds $C_L I$. The Schur node and step 1 therefore give $\|\chi_i\operatorname{Op}(a_i)f\|_{W^{s,2}}\leq C\|f\|_{W^{t,2}}$. The compact-symbol lemma also gives smooth compactly supported output. For real $f$, take its real part: each real derivative has norm at most that of the corresponding complex derivative, so the same estimate holds for $\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)f$.

proof.text: Write the fixed input partition as $(\theta_j)$. For every smooth section $u$, $\psi_i u=\sum_j\psi_i(\theta_j u)$. Apply the chart-overlap node at order $t$, with $K=\operatorname{supp}\theta_j$ in its source chart and target cutoff $\psi_i$. It bounds the coordinate $W^{t,2}$ norm of each summand by a fixed multiple of that of $\theta_j u$. There are finitely many pairs, so $\|\psi_i u\|_{W^{t,2}}\leq C_i\|u\|_{H^t}$. Each output from step 2 is supported in $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$. Apply the same node at order $s$ to each fixed output-partition cutoff to bound its global $H^s$ norm by its coordinate $W^{s,2}$ norm. At order zero the coordinate and integrated norms are equivalent: the smooth positive volume density and fibre-metric eigenvalues have positive minima and finite maxima on each compact support. Thus, summing the finitely many estimates from step 2, the symbol part $A_0$ satisfies $\|A_0u\|_{H^s}\leq C_0\|u\|_{H^t}$ on smooth sections.

proof.text: Treat the smooth-kernel term $R_K$ separately. In an output frame, for any localized coefficient and multi-index $\alpha$ the expected derivative is $\int_N \partial_x^\alpha(\rho(x)K(x,y))u(y)\,dV(y)$, where $\rho$ is its fixed output cutoff. Apply the dominated-integral derivative node inductively in $x$, taking the measure space $N$ and the finite-dimensional real target coefficient space. On a compact output neighbourhood all derivatives of the localized kernel are bounded by constants in operator norm relative to the input metric. The dominating function is $C|u(y)|$, integrable since $\int|u|\leq\operatorname{vol}(N)^{1/2}\|u\|_0$. The integrands and derivative integrands are measurable; their initial integrals exist by the same bound. This verifies every hypothesis for every differentiation. For smooth $u$ the resulting smooth coefficients have classical, hence distributional, derivatives equal to these integrals. Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\partial^\alpha(\rho R_Ku)(x)|\leq C_\alpha\operatorname{vol}(N)^{1/2}\|u\|_0$. Integrate the square over the compact output support and sum the finitely many coefficients and $|\alpha|\leq s$. Consequently $\|R_Ku\|_{H^s}\leq C_K\|u\|_0$. Each input localization controls its integrated $L^2$ norm by its order-$t$ norm, and $u=\sum\theta_j u$, so $\|u\|_0\leq C_t\|u\|_{H^t}$. The defining decomposition and the triangle inequality now give $\|Au\|_{H^s}\leq C\|u\|_{H^t}$ for every smooth $u$.

proof.text: Pass to an arbitrary section $u\in H^t(B)$ using the existing weak-Sobolev realization of bundle completions. That node identifies the completion with exactly the weak-derivative subspace in this item, supplies density of smooth sections and completeness, for the same norms up to equivalence. Its metric volume is allowed here: the given positive volume differs from it by a smooth strictly positive function, bounded above and below on compact $N$, so its integrated $L^2$ norm and the embedding into distributions agree up to equivalence. The localized higher-order norms are the same. For $t=0$ use the node's $L^2$ completion and measurable-section identification; for $s=0$ use the corresponding complete $L^2(C)$. The norms agree, not only the subspaces: if smooth $w_n$ converge in the completion to $w$, each localized derivative $\partial^\alpha(\theta_jw_n)$ is Cauchy in $L^2(\mathbf R^m)$, hence converges to some $g$; since $\theta_jw_n\to\theta_j j(w)$ in $L^2$, pairing with tests shows that $g$ is the distributional derivative $\partial^\alpha(\theta_j j(w))$. So the item's norm of $j(w)$ is the limit of the norms of $w_n$, the completion norm of $w$; smooth sections are dense in the item's $H^t(B)$ and $H^s(C)$ is complete for the item's norm. Choose smooth $u_n\to u$ in $H^t$. Step 4 applied to $u_n-u_k$ makes $Au_n$ Cauchy in $H^s(C)$, hence convergent to some $v$. Passing to limits in its norm estimate gives $\|v\|_{H^s}\leq C\|u\|_{H^t}$.

proof.text: It remains to identify $v$ with $Au$ in distributions. Input Sobolev convergence implies $L^2$ convergence by the continuous inclusion in the bundle-realization node (for $t=0$, by definition). For every smooth test section $\varphi$ of the dual bundle tensored with densities, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds $|\langle u_n-u,\varphi\rangle|$ by $C_\varphi\|u_n-u\|_0$, so $u_n\to u$ as distributions; the same reasoning gives $Au_n\to v$ as distributions from output Sobolev convergence. For a bounded set $S$ of tests in the current test-density definition, finitely many compact chart sets covering $N$ give uniform bounds on its order-zero coefficient seminorms, hence $\sup_{\varphi\in S}C_\varphi<\infty$. Thus both convergences hold uniformly on every such $S$, exactly the strong dual topology now specified in the symbol definition. The defining continuity $A:\mathcal D'(B)\to\mathcal D'(C)$ gives $Au_n\to Au$. Distributions are functionals on tests, so limits are unique and $Au=v$. The injective distributional realization of $L^2$ sections makes this equality an equality with the claimed Sobolev output class. The restriction is real-linear because $A$ is; the norm estimate proves boundedness. Taking $M_{A,t}=1+C$ makes the bound strictly positive, including zero operators and rank-zero bundles.
